cond_0001.intro: The primary focus of the position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management activities, performing data analysis and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. Data base development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills will be employed to work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Assures that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and assures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Assures charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Assures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient Administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to assist with contract compliance and identify savings opportunities that we are not taking advantage of at this time. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance, identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure that we are purchasing pharmaceuticals in the most cost efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interacts with hospital purchasing, materials handling and other departments responsively and productively to promote efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Interacts regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining the improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities:
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
Preferred Requirements
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background.

cond_0001.values: We value work that reflects care for people and consideration for its wider impact. We aim to make decisions in ways that are responsible, fair, and respectful.

Assures that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and assures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Assures charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Assures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient Administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to assist with contract compliance and identify savings opportunities that we are not taking advantage of at this time. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance, identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure that we are purchasing pharmaceuticals in the most cost efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interacts with hospital purchasing, materials handling and other departments responsively and productively to promote efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Interacts regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining the improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities:
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access
cond_0094.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
Preferred Requirements
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background.

cond_0133.intro: The primary focus of this position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management activities, performing data analysis, and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. Database development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills will be used to work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0133.responsibilities:
The statements below describe the general nature of work performed in this position. They are not an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Ensures billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and ensures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Ensures charges governed by APCs are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion, or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Ensures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to the pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with the GPO and wholesaler to support contract compliance and identify savings opportunities not currently being used; relays findings to Pharmacy Manager and Inventory Buyer to implement changes where possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance and identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons, and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing, and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports monthly to ensure pharmaceuticals are purchased in the most cost-efficient manner; communicates findings to Pharmacy Manager and Buyers and follows up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account and cost center as expenditures are processed, in accordance with accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interfaces with hospital purchasing, materials handling, and other departments to support efficient systems and resolve issues related to fiscal and clinical management.
Supplies drug usage information to the department management team and clinical specialists, identifies irregularities in spending, and provides recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data for use in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management on the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in planning and implementing change and maintaining productivity through attendance at staff meetings, committees, task forces, and projects.
Participates in the education of other healthcare professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Serves as accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintains system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Ensures appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Ensures compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Reviews and refines 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitors ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler; analyzes invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities: Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel and Access.
cond_0133.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associate's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years of experience in a healthcare setting.
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
Preferred Requirements
Direct experience in data analysis and/or a healthcare planning background.

cond_0191.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Assures that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and assures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Assures charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Assures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient Administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to assist with contract compliance and identify savings opportunities that we are not taking advantage of at this time. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance, identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure that we are purchasing pharmaceuticals in the most cost efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interacts with hospital purchasing, materials handling and other departments responsively and productively to promote efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Interacts regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining the improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities:
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access
cond_0191.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance required; advanced degree strongly preferred — with a minimum of 2 years of demonstrated expertise in pharmacy or at least 1 year of proven experience with financial reporting
OR
Associate's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance with a minimum of 4 years of demonstrated expertise in pharmacy or at least 3 years of proven experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma with National Pharmacy Technician Certification required within 15 months of hire and a minimum of 7 years of substantial experience in a healthcare setting.
Proven background in data analysis and/or healthcare planning strongly preferred.
Minimum 2 years of demonstrated expertise in a professional capacity in healthcare, with significant experience in Pharmacy preferred.
cond_0191.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0191.values: We value work that reflects care for people and consideration for its wider impact. We aim to make decisions in ways that are responsible, fair, and respectful.

cond_0237.intro: The primary focus of the position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management activities, performing data analysis and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. Data base development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills will be employed to work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0237.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Assures that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and assures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Assures charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Assures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient Administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to assist with contract compliance and identify savings opportunities that we are not taking advantage of at this time. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance, identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure that we are purchasing pharmaceuticals in the most cost efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interacts with hospital purchasing, materials handling and other departments responsively and productively to promote efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Interacts regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining the improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
cond_0237.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance (or equivalent practical experience), with around 2 years of experience in pharmacy or at least 1 year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associate's degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance (or equivalent practical experience), with around 4 years of experience in pharmacy or around 3 years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician (to be obtained within 15 months of hire, or willingness to obtain), with around 7 years of experience in a healthcare setting
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and Access
Preferred Requirements
Some background in data analysis and/or healthcare planning
Around 2 years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy

cond_0292.intro: The primary focus of the position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management activities, performing data analysis and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. Data base development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills will be employed to work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the financial and data logic behind pharmacy operations.
cond_0292.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Assures that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and assures accurate billing procedures are followed.
Assures charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Assures utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient Administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and makes recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Coordinates with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to assist with contract compliance and identify savings opportunities that we are not taking advantage of at this time. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance, identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure that we are purchasing pharmaceuticals in the most cost efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Interacts with hospital purchasing, materials handling and other departments responsively and productively to promote efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Interacts regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining the improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities:
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access
cond_0292.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
Preferred Requirements
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background.

The role draws on database development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills to direct work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0395.responsibilities:
Ensure that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Lead coordination with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely review medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and ensure accurate billing procedures are followed.
Ensure charges governed by APCs are handled correctly.
Drive the addition, deletion, or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintain all HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Ensure utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient administration of medications.
Lead coordination with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluate drug inventory levels and deliver recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitor purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Lead coordination with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to ensure contract compliance and identify savings opportunities not currently being utilized. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitor monthly budget variance and identify significant activity.
Generate a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compile data, produce profile comparisons, and generate reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Deliver data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing, and reimbursement.
Generate pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure pharmaceuticals are purchased in the most cost-efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to drive implementation of changes.
Document expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconcile department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectify errors within 30 days.
Identify irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and report to department Director.
Engage with hospital purchasing, materials handling, and other departments to drive efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Regularly engage with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and deliver recommendations for alternative products.
Support Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data for use in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Take ownership of departmental goals and objectives in collaboration with department management during development and implementation.
Lead participation in planning and implementing change and maintaining improved productivity through attendance and contribution in staff meetings, committees, task forces, and projects.
Contribute to the education of other healthcare professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Serve as accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Own maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Own documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Ensure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Ensure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler; analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
cond_0395.requirements:
Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background preferred.
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time.

cond_0468.intro: The primary focus of this position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by coordinating fiscal management activities, performing data analysis, and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. Database development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills will be used to work alongside clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0468.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Help ensure that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely reviews medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and helps ensure accurate billing procedures are followed.
Helps ensure charges governed by APC's are handled correctly.
Facilitates the addition, deletion or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintains all the HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Helps ensure utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient administration of medications.
Coordinates with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluates drug inventory levels and shares recommendations with the pharmacy manager.
Monitors purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Works alongside Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to support contract compliance and identify savings opportunities not currently being used. Relays those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitors monthly budget variance and identifies significant activity.
Generates a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compiles data, profiles comparisons, and generates reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Provides data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing, and reimbursement.
Generates pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to help ensure pharmaceuticals are purchased in the most cost-efficient manner. Shares those opportunities with Pharmacy Manager & Buyers and follows up to assist with implementation of changes.
Documents expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconciles department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectifies errors within 30 days.
Identifies irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and reports to department Director.
Works with hospital purchasing, materials handling, and other departments to support efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Coordinates regularly with the department management team and clinical specialists to share drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and provide recommendations for alternative products.
Supports Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data to be used in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Works with department management in the development and implementation of departmental goals and objectives.
Participates in the planning and implementing change and maintaining and improving productivity through attendance and participation in staff meetings, committees, task forces, and projects.
Participates in the education of other health-care professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Responsible for maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Responsible for documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Assure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Assure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler, analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time. Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds. Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Skills and Abilities: Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access.

Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and Four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or Three (3) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and Seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background preferred.
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.

cond_0539.intro: The primary focus of this position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by leading fiscal management activities, executing data analysis, and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. The role draws on database development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills to direct work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0539.responsibilities:
Ensure that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Lead coordination with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely review medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and ensure accurate billing procedures are followed.
Ensure charges governed by APCs are handled correctly.
Drive the addition, deletion, or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintain all HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Ensure utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient administration of medications.
Lead coordination with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluate drug inventory levels and deliver recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitor purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Lead coordination with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to ensure contract compliance and identify savings opportunities not currently being utilized. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitor monthly budget variance and identify significant activity.
Generate a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compile data, produce profile comparisons, and generate reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Deliver data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing, and reimbursement.
Generate pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure pharmaceuticals are purchased in the most cost-efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to drive implementation of changes.
Document expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconcile department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectify errors within 30 days.
Identify irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and report to department Director.
Engage with hospital purchasing, materials handling, and other departments to drive efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Regularly engage with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and deliver recommendations for alternative products.
Support Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data for use in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Take ownership of departmental goals and objectives in collaboration with department management during development and implementation.
Lead participation in planning and implementing change and maintaining improved productivity through attendance and contribution in staff meetings, committees, task forces, and projects.
Contribute to the education of other healthcare professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Serve as accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Own maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Own documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Ensure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Ensure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler; analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.
cond_0539.requirements:
Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background preferred.
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time.
Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds.
Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access

cond_0647.intro: The primary focus of this position is to support the operational efficiency of the Pharmacy Department by leading fiscal management activities, executing data analysis, and maintaining departmental statistics and reports. The role draws on database development, project management, cost accounting, and IT skills to direct work with clinical pharmacists, residents, medical staff, and pharmacy administration.
cond_0647.responsibilities:
Ensure that billing procedures performed by the department are accurate and timely.
Lead coordination with Patient Financial Services to review underpayments or denials.
Routinely review medications administered that are included on the transitional pass-through list and ensure accurate billing procedures are followed.
Ensure charges governed by APCs are handled correctly.
Drive the addition, deletion, or correction of charges to the charge master as needed.
Maintain all HCPCS changes and updates for Chargemaster.
Ensure utilization of all available indigent care programs for inpatient and outpatient administration of medications.
Lead coordination with Clinical Specialists to evaluate practice change opportunities that would allow inpatient medication administration to be switched to outpatient medication administration.
Evaluate drug inventory levels and deliver recommendations to pharmacy manager.
Monitor purchases for contract compliance and accurate pricing.
Lead coordination with Premier (GPO) and Amerisource Bergen to ensure contract compliance and identify savings opportunities not currently being utilized. Relay those items to Pharmacy Manager & Inventory Buyer to implement changes when possible.
Monitor monthly budget variance and identify significant activity.
Generate a year-end report of budget versus expended dollars based on reconciliation of budget with the general ledger, for each cost center by account.
Compile data, produce profile comparisons, and generate reports related to current expenses to serve as the basis for the asking budget.
Deliver data to support department performance improvement activities related to drug utilization, purchasing, billing, and reimbursement.
Generate pharmacy spend advisor reports on a monthly basis to ensure pharmaceuticals are purchased in the most cost-efficient manner. Communicate those opportunities to Pharmacy Manager & Buyers. Follow up to drive implementation of changes.
Document expenditure activity by account by cost centers as expenditures are processed and according to accepted accounting practices.
Reconcile department current expenditure documentation with the hospital general ledger and rectify errors within 30 days.
Identify irregular spending and system failures related to current expense activity and report to department Director.
Engage with hospital purchasing, materials handling, and other departments to drive efficient systems interface and problem resolution related to fiscal and clinical management.
Regularly engage with the department management team and clinical specialists to supply drug usage information, identify irregularities in spending, and deliver recommendations for alternative products.
Support Pharmacy, Nutrition and Therapeutics Committee functions by providing financial data for use in the drug evaluation process, including opportunities for therapeutic interchange of medications.
Take ownership of departmental goals and objectives in collaboration with department management during development and implementation.
Lead participation in planning and implementing change and maintaining improved productivity through attendance and contribution in staff meetings, committees, task forces, and projects.
Contribute to the education of other healthcare professionals as it pertains to appropriate use and billing of medications.
Serve as accountable agent for 340B compliance.
Own maintenance and testing of tracking software.
Own documentation of policy and procedures.
Maintain system databases to reflect changes in the drug formulary or product specifications.
Ensure appropriate safeguards and system integrity.
Ensure compliance with 340B program requirements of qualified patients, drugs, providers, vendors, payers, and locations.
Review and refine 340B cost savings report detailing purchasing and replacement practices, as well as dispensing patterns.
Monitor ordering processes, integrating most current pricing from wholesaler; analyze invoices, shipping, and inventory processes.

Bachelor degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and two (2) years of experience in pharmacy or one (1) year of experience with financial reporting
OR
Associates degree in Information Technology, Business Management, Hospital Administration, Accounting, or Finance and four (4) years of experience in pharmacy or three (3) years of experience with financial reporting
OR
High School Diploma and Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician within 15 months of hire and seven (7) years' experience in a healthcare setting
Direct experience in data analysis and/or health care planning background preferred.
Two (2) years of experience in a professional capacity in healthcare, preferably in Pharmacy.
While performing the duties of this position, the employee is required to walk and stand for long periods of time.
Must be able to lift 30 pounds and must be able to push 50 pounds.
Dexterity required to finger, handle, and reach.
Extensive working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Excel & Access
